title: Pawnee County Sheriff Confronts Cleveland Police Officers Over a Search Warrant
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Cleveland, Oklahoma — Newly released body-camera video shows Cleveland Police planned to serve a search warrant inside Pawnee County. Because Cleveland officers were cross-deputized, they were legally allowed to work cases there. According to Cleveland Police, their chief notified the Pawnee County Sheriff’s Office two weeks before the warrant was to be served, asking whether the sheriff’s deputies were working any related investigation. The sheriff’s office reportedly said no, and Cleveland officers continued preparing the warrant, which a judge later approved. On the night of October 28, 2025, Cleveland officers gathered at their police station for a briefing before heading out to execute the warrant. A Pawnee County deputy had been told the night before and was on the way to attend the briefing. Moments after the officers met, Sheriff Shawn Price arrived unexpectedly at the station, upset that he had only learned about the warrant 15 minutes beforehand. Price confronted the officers, raising his voice and questioning why they were moving forward without involving him in the planning. He later said that if something went wrong during the operation, he would be held responsible for an event he had no role in coordinating. The confrontation was captured on body-camera video and led Cleveland Police to revoke their cross-deputation agreement with the Sheriff’s Office, meaning officers are no longer taking calls in the County. Although the disagreement escalated, the District Attorney reviewed the footage and found that no crime occurred.
